column1: # The ledger for environment centos-9-glibc2.34 (run.sh names this host's: os id, os version, glibc).
# Measured with `reverie-examples/e2e/run.sh --write-ledger` on a CentOS Stream 9 devserver (glibc
# 2.34), all seven backends; two runs gave identical rows. A row names a program's first difference
# only. cell<TAB>backend<TAB>verdict<TAB>signature<TAB>issue (full URL); * for any cell or signature.
# Until their own issues are filed, the rows link the audit's tracking issue. The liteinst and
# in-guest-trap rows were re-measured on 2026-11-02 after runtime descriptor isolation (a461e8bf),
# with run.sh --backends ptrace,liteinst,in-guest-trap; two runs gave identical rows.
# Every program runs with LC_ALL=C (compare.rs, LOCALE; README.md, Locale). All rows were measured
# again with that pin on 2026-11-21 on devbig014 (kernel 7.1.3), run.sh with the four first-party
# backends; two runs gave identical rows. The pin changed twelve rows: the four /proc/self/maps rows,
# the six shell rows and the two python3 rows of the in-guest backends.
# ptrace: the tool never sees the rt_sigreturn that ends a signal handler.
sh-fork
sh-pipe
# ptrace: reverie-ptrace's two private pages (0x71000000 and 0x71001000) are listed first in
# /proc/self/maps, 41 bytes each, and a read of the listing returns whole lines up to one page. So
# a first read that natively returns the whole listing returns 82 bytes more (grep), and one that
# natively stops at the page boundary returns 82 bytes less the native lines pushed past it (awk).
# The counts follow the libraries each program maps and the kernel's special mappings: measure again
# after a package or kernel update that changes those lines.
grep-passwd
awk
# KVM: rseq answers ENOSYS (reverie-kvm refuses it), the first difference on every program.
# liteinst: the tool lives in the example preload and starts after the loader's calls (compare.rs,
# LATE_START). Then: the shell's getrandom is not seen by the tool; awk's fcntl(F_GETFL) lacks
# O_LARGEFILE; dd's and perl's first visible calls do not appear in the native record in order (no
# aligned start); grep's first read of /proc/self/maps returns more, and more reads follow, because
# the runtime's mappings are listed (natively one read returns the whole listing; the in-guest first
# read returned the same count with preload paths of 1 and 84 characters; later, grep's sigaltstack
# install is refused with EPERM unseen by the tool, so grep runs without its SIGSEGV handler, issue
# 5097); sort's rt_sigaction queries (NULL new action) never reach the tool (issue 5096); and a
# guest's own execve is refused with EOPNOTSUPP, the in-guest runtime not forwarding it, so python3
# (run through env) exits 126: in the C locale that execve is the first call of env's the tool sees,
# and the late-start alignment cannot place it (no aligned start; issue 5094; sh-fork and sh-pipe
# fail the same way behind their earlier first difference, issue 5095).
grep-passwd
sort-passwd
python3
sh-builtin
sh-fork
sh-pipe
awk
dd-zero
perl
